data.name: Devindar
data.gender_notes: Devindar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Devindar is derived from Sanskrit words ‘deva’ (god) and ‘indra’ (Thunderbolt). This name is given to a boy, signifying the divine power and strength of the deity Indra, the god of rain and thunder. The name Devindar carries the meaning “God's Indr (Thunderbolt)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devindar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's indr (thunderbolt) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Devindar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Indr (Thunderbolt).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devindar total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Devindra was a famous king of the Haihayas dynasty in the 13th century CE. He is mentioned in various Hindu texts and inscriptions, and is remembered for his military prowess and his patronage of temples and scholars.

Another reference to Devindra can be found in the Puranic literature. In the Bhagavata Purana, there is a mention of a sage named Devindra who was a devotee of Lord Vishnu. He performed severe penances and was blessed with a vision of the deity. This Devindra is considered a manifestation of Lord Vishnu himself.
